judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not challenge the 'all expanding' claim in the abstract against the BGV source. Major comment 3 discusses the NEC assumption and loitering universe but focuses on the energy-condition refinement, not the over-generalisation from 'inflationary' to 'all expanding'. No reviewer flag clearly corresponds to this specific scope-qualifier change.

The review discusses scope and assumptions of the BGV theorem and even mentions the loitering-universe subtlety, but it does not specifically flag the abstract claim that BGV shows 'all expanding spacetimes' are past-incomplete or challenge that statement against Borde-Guth-Vilenkin.

The reviewer uses the injected 'expanding spacetimes' terminology in their own summary, indicating they did not find the characterization of the BGV theorem to be an over-generalization. Their comments regarding the abstract (Major Comment 2) concern attribution and novelty relative to prior work, not the accuracy of the BGV theorem statement itself.

The reviewer does not flag the abstract's claim that 'all expanding spacetimes are generically geodesically past-incomplete' as an over-generalization of the BGV theorem. The reviewer discusses the loitering universe counterexample and the NEC assumption in Section 1, but never challenges the abstract's broadened claim as contradicting or mischaracterising the actual BGV theorem, which applies to inflationary (H_av > 0) spacetimes rather than all expanding spacetimes.

The reviewer does not mention any inconsistency in the prefactor of the ln term in the timelike F(gamma) expression, nor flag any discrepancy between eq:FTimelike and the proof block restatement involving 3/2 vs 2/3.
The reviewer notes algebraic/sign issues in Eqs. (43) and (52), but does not mention the timelike F(gamma) prefactor, the conflicting values 3/2 versus 2/3, or any inconsistency with Eq. FTimelike.

The reviewer flags algebraic clarity in equation (52) and a potential sign inconsistency between equations (43) and (46), but makes no mention of the 3/2 to 2/3 prefactor swap in the theorem's proof or the internal numerical contradiction it creates.

The reviewer does not flag any inconsistency between the coefficient 2/3 in the proof block and the 3/2 in eq. (64)/(FTimelike). The mention of Eq. (43) sign check and Eq. (52) algebra is unrelated to this specific numerical mismatch.

The reviewer does not flag an error in the Lorentz factor definition (gamma^2 = 1/(1+v^2) vs the canonical 1/(1-v^2)). No comment addresses a sign error in the denominator of the boost factor equation.
There is no comment identifying the Lorentz-factor definition gamma^2 = 1/(1-v^2) or flagging an incorrect plus sign in its denominator. The cited minor algebra/sign comments concern other equations.

The reviewer does not flag the sign error in the definition of the Lorentz factor (1 + v^2 vs 1 - v^2). While they ask for more explicit algebra to verify a downstream result in Minor Comment 10, they do not identify the foundational definition error.

The reviewer does not flag the sign error in the Lorentz factor definition (Eq. 10), where the denominator was changed from (1-v^2) to (1+v^2). The reviewer comments on Eq. (43) sign consistency and Eq. (52) algebra, but never mentions the canonical Lorentz factor formula or its denominator sign.

The reviewer's minor comment on Eq. (27) mentions 'since H_- < 0 and τ < t < T' but does not specifically flag that tau is incorrectly defined as the contracting phase when the downstream integrals treat it as the expanding phase. The comment addresses sign convention in N_-, not the mislabeling of tau's definition.

The reviewer comments on Eq. (27) sign convention for N_- and on bounce assumptions, but does not specifically identify the internal inconsistency that tau is defined as the contracting-phase duration while later used as the upper limit for the expanding-phase integral H_+ from 0 to tau.

The reviewer discusses the integration limits and sign of the cycle segments in Minor Comment 3, but they follow the intended physical logic (treating tau as the end of expansion) and fail to notice that the text explicitly (and incorrectly) defined tau as the duration of the contracting phase.

The reviewer does not flag any inconsistency between the definition of τ as the 'contracting phase' duration and its use in the downstream calculations (Eqs. 24, 26, 27) where it labels the expanding phase. The reviewer mentions Eq. (27) regarding sign conventions but does not identify the τ-labeling inconsistency.
